correctness.rationale: For a fixed cycle of length \(c\), the rooted-forest determinant yields exactly \(c n^{m-1}\) forests, and a forced-leaf deletion bijection yields the full conditional empty-box law. Explicit increments of the conditional mean establish strict negative regression for \(n\ge4\). The truncated Poisson CLT and a bounded martingale-difference CLT for vacant boxes establish the joint independent half-normal/Gaussian limit. The quadratic conditional mean response and uniform integrability yield covariance asymptotic coefficient \(-1/(e\sqrt{2\pi})\). Standalone exhaustive finite enumeration verifies all bivariate tables and mixed moments for \(3\le n\le7\); infinite claims use the analytic proof.

evidence: Ben-Naim–Krapivsky (2004) focuses on mean numbers of components of size k in an evolving random multigraph and critical-time asymptotics.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither examined theorem concerns the same uniform conditioned simple unicyclic law, so they do not dominate the joint distribution, strict negative regression, or joint central limit with second-order covariance. General conditioned random-graph probability theory could imply a marginal CLT, but marginal results alone do not imply this exact dependence statement.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The complete theorem combines precise conditional factorial-binomial moments, strictly decreasing conditional mean across every cycle length, independent half-normal/Gaussian leading fluctuations, and a negative sqrt(n)-scale covariance. The cited prior claims are not logically strong enough to imply all four together without additional combinatorial and probabilistic derivations. Their shared parameters and standard building blocks alone do not constitute coverage.

value.rationale: Two intrinsic and motivated random-graph statistics have an exact finite conditional law, a universal strictly negative regression for every increasing cycle function, and a counterintuitive independent first-order scaling limit with negative sqrt(n)-order raw covariance. This provides a natural structural dependence classification rather than a routine isolated enumeration.
